mcqs.learning_point: Identify objects at rest and in motion relative to a reference point
mcqs.question: A book is lying on a table while a car is moving on a road. An observer standing on the sidewalk watches both. Which statement correctly identifies the state of each object relative to the observer?

options.A: Both the book and the car are at rest
options.B: Both the book and the car are in motion
options.C: The book is at rest and the car is in motion
options.D: The book is in motion and the car is at rest

mcqs.answer: The book is at rest and the car is in motion
mcqs.explanation: From the observer’s point of view, the book does not change its position, so it is at rest. The car changes its position over time, so it is in motion. Option C states this correctly. Options A and B ignore the difference, and Option D reverses the states, which is a common misconception when the reference point is not considered.

mcqs.question: A student watches three objects: (i) a ball rolling down a slope, (ii) a ceiling fan rotating, (iii) a pendulum swinging back and forth. Which option correctly matches each object with its type of motion?

options.A: (i) Linear motion, (ii) Rotational motion, (iii) Periodic motion
options.B: (i) Rotational motion, (ii) Linear motion, (iii) Periodic motion
options.C: (i) Periodic motion, (ii) Linear motion, (iii) Rotational motion
options.D: (i) Linear motion, (ii) Periodic motion, (iii) Rotational motion

mcqs.answer: (i) Linear motion, (ii) Rotational motion, (iii) Periodic motion
mcqs.explanation: A ball rolling down a slope moves along a straight (or curved) path – linear motion. A ceiling fan spins around an axis – rotational motion. A pendulum repeatedly moves back and forth – periodic motion. Option A captures all three correctly; the other options mix up the categories.

mcqs.learning_point: Describe motion using distance and time
mcqs.question: Student A runs 120 m in 15 s, while Student B runs 150 m in 20 s. Which statement correctly compares their speeds?

options.A: Student A is faster because he covers more distance in less time
options.B: Student B is faster because he covers more distance overall
options.C: Both students have the same speed
options.D: Student A is faster because his speed (8 m/s) is greater than Student B's speed (7.5 m/s)

mcqs.answer: Student A is faster because his speed (8 m/s) is greater than Student B's speed (7.5 m/s)
mcqs.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time. Student A: 120 m ÷ 15 s = 8 m/s. Student B: 150 m ÷ 20 s = 7.5 m/s. Since 8 m/s > 7.5 m/s, Student A is faster. Option D gives the correct calculation; Options A and B are vague and Option C is false.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify periodic motion in everyday examples
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday phenomena best illustrates periodic motion?

options.A: A car accelerating on a highway
options.B: The swinging pendulum of a wall clock
options.C: Water flowing continuously from a tap
options.D: A person walking straight across a room

mcqs.answer: The swinging pendulum of a wall clock
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals. The pendulum of a clock swings back and forth in a regular, repeating pattern, making it a classic example of periodic motion. A car accelerating, water flowing, and walking straight are not repetitive in a regular cycle, so options A, C, and D are incorrect.
